headline: Solar panels transform Kubuqi Desert into hub of green development and ecological restoration
article:
HOHHOT (Xinhua) -- In the Kubuqi Desert in Ordos, Inner Mongolia autonomous region, large arrays of deep blue solar panels are redefining the landscape, transforming a once-barren stretch of sand into a dynamic hub of green development and ecological restoration.

The photovoltaic arrays stretch across the shifting dunes, presenting a striking visual contrast to the traditional image of the desert. Beneath the panels, a distinct microclimate has emerged. The shade provided by the solar boards, coupled with a noticeable reduction in wind speeds, has significantly altered the local environment. This physical barrier effectively curbs groundwater evaporation, creating favorable conditions for vegetation to take root and thrive in the arid soil.

Data from the desert reclamation projects indicate that the solar panels cut groundwater evaporation by about 20 to 30 percent. This measurable improvement in soil moisture supports the growth of forage and hardy plants, which in turn help consolidate the sand and reverse desertification. The "photovoltaic power generation plus desert reclamation" model establishes a virtuous cycle where clean energy infrastructure directly facilitates ecological restoration.

Beyond its environmental impact, the initiative has become a vital engine for improving local livelihoods. The integration of solar farms into the desert has opened diverse income opportunities for residents. Local communities now benefit from land leasing, construction jobs, and contract farming associated with the maintenance and operation of the solar arrays. By linking clean energy production with agricultural and pastoral activities, the project aligns with broader rural revitalization goals, ensuring that the transition to green development brings tangible economic benefits to the people living on the edge of the desert.

Through this innovative approach, the Kubuqi Desert demonstrates a practical, win-win model. It highlights how the pursuit of clean energy and the imperative of desertification control can advance hand in hand. As the blue panels continue to harness the abundant solar resources, they simultaneously nurture a recovering ecosystem and foster sustainable livelihoods. The project narratives consistently emphasize that clean energy and ecological restoration are not mutually exclusive, but rather complementary forces. Ultimately, this model offers a constructive blueprint for balancing energy transition with ecological conservation, proving that green development can yield both environmental and economic dividends.
